Kimberly — forwarding Novus' redlines (attached). Procurement is pushing for sign this week. High-level items they flagged that will need legal language:

1) Output title: Novus requests assignment of title to "Customer Generated Output" used in their product. They want explicit "title to output" language, not just a license.
2) Training / retrain use: They want a carve-out preventing any use of outputs or customer content to train/fine-tune Redwood models unless Novus opts in and we agree separate commercial terms.
3) Feedback license: They propose we accept a very narrow feedback license limited to anonymized telemetry and product improvement, time-limited, and revocable.

My suggested commercial compromise (to speed procurement):
- Define "Customer Generated Output" as customer inputs + outputs produced by Redwood when configured by the customer, excluding Redwood models, weights, and system-reserved telemetry.
- Provide Novus a perpetual, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce and distribute Customer Generated Output for their productization purposes (i.e., to include in their app). But exclude rights to require assignment of our underlying models or weights.
- For training: add an explicit opt-in checkbox on the Order Form ("Customer consents to Redwood using CUSTOMER DATA for model training — yes/no") and default to NO. Any opt-in should trigger a negotiated SOW/compensation.
- For feedback: offer a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use aggregated/anonymized telemetry for product improvement, with a 30-day notice if we intend to start using non-aggregated examples; include retention limits (e.g., 90 days for raw telemetry).

Can Legal please review the above and suggest clean Order Form/MSA language. Also flag any operational implications (telemetry retention, export controls, DMZ). Novus will likely ask for some attribution language too.

Attachments: Novus_OrderForm_redline.docx, redline_summary.pdf

Thanks —
Jasmine

Team — reviewed Novus' redlines and Jasmine's suggested compromise. Below are proposed legal edits and reasoning (high level). I recommend we offer a tracked Order Form counter that implements most of Jasmine's commercial points with clarified definitions and an explicit fallback policy.

Key redline suggestions (MSA + Order Form):
1) Definitions
- "Customer Generated Output": define as "Output (text, code, images, data) generated by the Service in response to Customer Input under the Customer's account and configuration; excludes underlying model parameters, pre-trained weights, and Redwood internal tooling."

2) Output rights
- Offer: Customer gets a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, and distribute Customer Generated Output for Customer's business purposes.
- Reject: assignment of title to Redwood's service or models. We can consider assignment of title to specific Delivered Output (e.g., final compiled assets) if commercially required, but avoid broad assignment language.

3) Training and Feedback
- Default rule: Redwood will not use Customer Input or Customer Generated Output to train or improve Redwood's models unless Customer opts in via the Order Form (explicit opt-in).
- Opt-in: if checked, training use limited by an SOW or Order Form clause that includes scope, notice, and compensation.
- Feedback license: propose narrow clause: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use aggregated and de-identified telemetry and usage data solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Service. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Generated Output to train models to provide competitive services to the Customer without separate written agreement."

4) Telemetry & retention
- Operational controls: limit retention of raw telemetry to 90 days unless otherwise agreed; provide definition of aggregated/de-identified data; include an audit right for enterprise SKUs.

5) Escalation/fallback policy
- If explicit training consent absent, Redwood may use aggregated metrics and system telemetry for capacity/performance optimization only. Any move to use non-aggregated examples requires 30 days' notice and Customer opt-in.

6) Commercial levers
- If Novus requires assignment of title for discrete categories of outputs, route to commercial (Laura) for uplift/commitment. We can offer a narrow assignment for certain "Delivered Outputs" for a fee.

I think this preserves our IP, addresses Novus' procurement needs, and provides a clean opt-in operational path. Laura/Dev: flag any product/ops constraints (export, retention, telemetry pipelines) so we can include them in the SOW.

If all agree, I'll prepare redline markup for the Order Form and a short addendum (one page) that implements the opt-in and retention terms.

- Kimberly

Hi Sara — thanks for the patience. Legal has reviewed and we've prepared a focused counter-proposal that we think meets Novus' objectives while protecting operational IP. Summary of our position and proposed edits: 

1) Customer Generated Output: we will grant Novus a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, reproduce and distribute Customer Generated Output (as defined). We are not assigning title to Redwood models or service.

2) Training use: default = NO. The Order Form will include an explicit opt-in checkbox to permit Redwood to use Customer Data/Outputs for model training; opt-in will trigger a separate SOW and compensation.

3) Feedback & telemetry: we will accept a narrow feedback license limited to aggregated/de-identified telemetry for product improvement. Raw telemetry retention will be limited to 90 days unless Novus requests extended retention in writing. Redwood will provide notice 30 days before using any non-aggregated examples for model improvement and will require Customer opt-in for those uses.

4) Commercial path for assignment: if Novus requires assignment of title for discrete Delivered Outputs, we can discuss a commercial uplift — Laura can take the lead on pricing/commitment language.

Next steps / action items:
- I've attached the redline markup of the Order Form and a one-page addendum that implements the opt-in checkbox and retention terms. Please review: redline_summary.pdf and Novus_OrderForm_RedwoodCounter.docx.
- If Novus accepts in principle, Laura will prepare a DocuSign envelope and commercial terms for the assignment option (if requested).
- Request: confirm by EOD Fri whether Novus will accept the opt-in approach or will require assignment language. Procurement prefers a yes/no on the opt-in to close.
